behaviors.source: GH #97 AC1; prd.md D12 ("routeFinalReviewFinding gains the writing stage id as an input… returns stageId = the last stage that ran"); src/final-evaluation.ts:429-436, :438-455, :39, :49, :42-48, :67
behaviors.given: routeFinalReviewFinding taking context: { candidateTreeId: string; writingStageIds: readonly string[] }, where writingStageIds is declared on the parameter to hold only the stages that actually changed the tree, in the order they ran — a stage that ran and left the tree byte-identical contributes no id, which is why production's noopPostApprovalWritingStage never appears
behaviors.when: a FinalReviewFinding with repair: "RESTORE" is routed with writingStageIds of [CLEANER_STAGE_ID], of [CLEANER_STAGE_ID, POST_APPROVAL_WRITING_STAGE_ID], and of [], and separately a non-RESTORE finding is routed
behaviors.then: the RESTORE route returns { target: "writing-stage", repair: "RESTORE", stageId } with stageId = the last id in writingStageIds — "cleaner" for [CLEANER_STAGE_ID], "post-approval-writing" for the two-id list because that stage wrote last, and "post-approval-writing" for [] by the pre-slice fallback so no caller loses a route by not knowing about a cleaner; the last-id rule is well-defined only against the list contract B-02 satisfies, and the committed cleaner's id is last even though the cleaner runs first (src/final-evaluation.ts:42-48) precisely because the no-op stage contributes nothing; a non-RESTORE repair still routes to generator-loop with generatorRoundsConsumed: 1 and finalEvaluationAttemptsConsumed: 0, and the FinalReviewRoute shape at :429-436 is otherwise unchanged
behaviors.observableResult: src/final-evaluation.test.ts's [behavior:B-01] unit tests (no git, no pipeline — the file's existing posture) assert the three stageId values for the three lists and the unchanged generator-loop route with its two round counts

behaviors.source: GH #97 AC1; prd.md D12; src/orchestrator.ts:7701-7703, :7772-7776; src/final-evaluation.ts:39, :49, :67
behaviors.given: the one routeFinalReviewFinding call site (src/orchestrator.ts:7701-7703) and the three tree ids it already holds — the accepted tree, the cleaner's inputTreeId/outputTreeId, and currentFinalTreeId
behaviors.when: writingStageIds is built for the route
behaviors.then: it appends, in run order, one id per stage that changed the tree it was handed: CLEANER_STAGE_ID when cleaner.ran && cleaner.outputTreeId !== cleaner.inputTreeId, then POST_APPROVAL_WRITING_STAGE_ID when currentFinalTreeId !== stageInputTreeId, where stageInputTreeId is the cleaner's outputTreeId if the cleaner committed and the accepted tree otherwise. So the committed-cleaner case under production's no-op stage is exactly [CLEANER_STAGE_ID] and B-01's last-id rule names the cleaner; a test-injected stage that writes on top of a committed cleaner yields [CLEANER_STAGE_ID, POST_APPROVAL_WRITING_STAGE_ID] and names the stub, which is correct because the stub wrote last; neither writing yields [] and B-01's fallback keeps the pre-slice route. The two ids stay distinct constants, and the comparisons are the same three tree ids B-12 tiles its spans from, computed once at this call site, so the route and the change-summary attribution cannot disagree about who wrote
behaviors.observableResult: src/final-evaluation.test.ts asserts the pure list builder returns [CLEANER_STAGE_ID] for a committed cleaner with an unmoved post-approval checkpoint, [] for neither writing, and the two-id list when both wrote; the spawned S3 scenario in src/qa-orchestration-gates.test.ts corroborates it against real trees — the RESTORE it produces is handled by the cleaner branch, not the stub

behaviors.source: GH #97 AC4; prd.md D10 item 3, D11 ("model time (sum of stage-duration.durationMs)"), prd.md:514, :569-573, :741-742; src/logger.ts:104-135, :116, :118-135; src/run-events.ts:347-371; src/run-journal.ts:133-168; src/stage-durations.ts:57-63; src/orchestrator.ts:6862, :6928, :7559
behaviors.given: a run directory whose events.jsonl carries quality-stage-policy, quality-stage-attempt and stage-duration lines, and separately a run directory with no events
behaviors.when: readQualityStageOutcomes(runDir) — new in src/logger.ts, modelled on readAdvisoryGateOutcomes (:118-135) — reads it
behaviors.then: it reads events.jsonl alone and returns one QualityStageOutcome per (ghIssue, stage): enabled (from quality-stage-policy), outcome, rounds used, round limit, elapsed ms (sum of the stage's quality-stage-attempt durationMs), model ms, gate ids, cache-reused gate ids, and the final decision (reuse / evaluate from final-evaluation-reuse or its absence). Model ms is the sum of the stage-duration events already on the stream — the RunEventPayload member at src/run-events.ts:347-371 carrying ghIssue, sliceNumber?, agent, round?, durationMs, history, ratioToMedian? — matched on ghIssue plus agent, with agent === "cleaner" for stage "cleaner" and agent === "evaluator-final" for stage "final-evaluation", the two literal roles the orchestrator's phase events already carry (:6862, :6928, :7559). Those events are derived, not hand-emitted: RunJournal.observeStageDuration (src/run-journal.ts:133-168) pairs each phase-ended with the newest unmatched phase-started under stageInvocationKey (src/stage-durations.ts:57-63) and appends the line, so this reader adds no writer and src/stage-durations.ts stays read-only. A stage whose phase-ended never arrived contributes no sample and its model ms is 0. A run directory with no events or no such event returns [] rather than throwing, for the reason :116 gives
behaviors.observableResult: src/logger.test.ts unit tests seed events.jsonl by hand with one quality-stage-policy line, three quality-stage-attempt lines across two slices, and stage-duration lines carrying agent "cleaner" and "evaluator-final", then assert the returned entries field by field — summed elapsed, summed model ms, rounds used, gate ids, cache-reused gate ids — plus model ms 0 when the stage-duration lines are absent and [] for a directory with no events

behaviors.source: GH #97 AC4 ("preserves every stage's attempt evidence end to end"); #87 B-09; src/artifacts.ts:758-775, name built at :772; src/orchestrator.ts:6962-6972, archiveDir at :6968
behaviors.given: a slice whose cleaner committed on its third cleaner round inside its first generator round
behaviors.when: the archived round evidence is located
behaviors.then: the file is named cleaner-log-r1-a3.log — the stem src/artifacts.ts:772 builds from the caller's slots, where round is the generator round and attempt is the cleaner round (src/orchestrator.ts:6962-6972) — inside whatever directory that call site passes as archiveDir, the reviewArchiveDir value it already holds (:6968) under .afk/artifacts/<run-slug>/slice-<n>/. The directory segment beneath that prefix is deliberately not pinned by this contract, because the builder that composes it lives in the out-of-scope src/artifacts.ts; the assertion resolves it from the run's artifact tree instead of hard-coding it. No argument re-mapping is authorized: a re-map would silently rename every already-archived round's log
behaviors.observableResult: S3 asserts the surviving archived log has the stem cleaner-log-r1-a3.log, with its directory discovered under the run's .afk/artifacts/<run-slug>/slice-<n>/ tree rather than written into the assertion
